key_insight: Support-constrained offline reinforcement learning improves estimated pediatric ECMO policy value while staying closer to clinician behavior than unconstrained FQI.
engineering_relevance: Restricting policy optimization to data-supported actions and falling back to clinicians offers a practical safeguard for learning from limited, high-stakes clinical data.
method: Use Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC) to optimize only over empirically supported state-action pairs.
Default to the clinician baseline in low-data regions.
Assess policies using Fitted Q-Evaluation, clinician-action disagreement, and a unified Balance Score.
evidence_signal: Across 78 pediatric trajectories covering over 6,000 hours, FQI-SC improved Balance Score by 38% and reduced clinician-action disagreement by 71% versus FQI, while exceeding imitation learning by 1.28 estimated FQE value units.
watch_item: Offline value estimates and clinician agreement do not establish clinical safety or reduced neurological injury; prospective validation is needed.
paper_title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
